data.description:
WHAT. The AS-5 chat export ('./apps/chat/chat export', run by the tick after every merge, committed to master as 'records: chat export YYYY-MM-DD') writes one JSONL file per conversation into apps/chat/data/export/. AS-6 excluded private channels (#board, #bizdev) outright: no file, no counts. It deliberately left DMs exporting (store.js:829-841 — the WHERE clause is NOT (type = 'channel' AND visibility = 'private'), type-scoped on purpose, even though every DM row is visibility='private' at store.js:350). Result: every DM between the board member and an employee ships to public master — nine files today: dm-agent~{ceo-carla,cto-owen,designer-sofia,developer-lena,developer-marcus,qa-priya,researcher-elliot,researcher-nadia,ux-jonah}~~human~forrest.jsonl. The board found it in a metawork review of what the public repo exposes (#board msg 559, 2026-09-07) and directed: treat DMs involving human:forrest exactly like the private channels — hidden means hidden, including git.

WHY NOW. The leak recurs on every tick that exports (every merge), so every day it stands adds lines to public history that cannot later be un-published. CLAUDE.md 'Operational record commits' already records the directive as 'pending the implementing task'; this is that task.

DECISIONS (CTO, owning the scoping per the board's request):
1. GENERALIZE TO ANY HUMAN PARTICIPANT, not the literal id. Exclude every DM where at least one member identity has kind='human' (equivalently: a dm_key component with the 'human:' prefix — dm_key is the two ids sorted and joined by '|', see dmKeyFor at store.js:103). Rationale: the rule the board stated is about a person's private conversations, not about one string. human:forrest is the only human today; hard-coding it would silently leak the first DM with a second human (advisor, second board member, a future customer contact) and nobody would notice until the next metawork audit. Cost of generalizing: zero extra code paths, one predicate. Agent-agent DMs (e.g. ceo-carla~~cto-owen) KEEP exporting — those are company-internal work record and the board asked only for his DMs.
2. SAME TREATMENT AS AS-6, BOTH HALVES: (a) no file is written for an excluded DM, and (b) an excluded DM moves no number in the CLI's 'N conversations, M messages' summary — the count a human-DM-free DB would report is the count reported. identities.jsonl still lists human identities (it does today; identity existence is not conversation content, and #board's members are already visible there).
3. THE BRANCH DELETES DATA FILES. The implementing code branch 'git rm's the nine committed apps/chat/data/export/dm-*~~human~forrest.jsonl files. This is explicitly sanctioned: the 'records commits touch only apps/chat/data/export/' scope rule is about not MIXING records with code in a records commit — a task branch deleting export artifacts that the task's own guard now forbids is the task's work, and it must land in the same merge as the guard, or the next export re-creates the files (the exporter writes every file it emits; the deletion only sticks because the guard stops emitting them). Do the removal as its own commit on the branch ('AS-N: remove the nine committed human:forrest DM exports') so the diff reviewer sees code and data separately.
4. HISTORY IS NOT REWRITTEN. Verbatim from the board: 'Do not rewrite history — the content is already public, this governs future exports.' No filter-branch, no force-push, no amend of anything pushed. The nine files remain in git history; the board accepted that. Force-push is needs_human by standing rule anyway.
5. DETERMINISM CONTRACT (store.js:800-807) holds for every file that continues to exist: byte-identical prefix plus appended lines. The header line gains no new key (same reasoning as AS-6). Deleting a file is not rewriting one.
6. IMPLEMENTER: developer-marcus — the internal-tools default (CLAUDE.md, DM msg 230), and he is the free lane: Lena holds AS-45 cycle 4 and is the implementer of record on AS-75 (in review, with AS-84 queued to her after merge). Reviewer: whichever QA did not review the branch's neighbours — Ruben is on AS-45 cycle 4, so Priya by default; the orchestrator assigns at review time.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (a floor — the reviewer probes past it, M6):
AC-1. exportFiles() emits no dm-*.jsonl for any DM with a human participant. Falsifier (M4): a test seeds, in one fresh store, (i) a DM between agent:developer-marcus and human:forrest with two messages and (ii) a sibling DM between agent:developer-marcus and agent:qa-priya with one message; asserts no filename contains '~~human~' or starts with 'dm-human~', asserts no exported line contains either human-DM message body, AND asserts the sibling agent-agent DM file exists with its header + 1 message line. With the store.js WHERE clause reverted to its AS-6 form, this test MUST be observed red naming the human DM file — the review comment records the observed red, not an argument that it would go red.
AC-2. The CLI summary reports the same 'N conversations, M messages' a DB without the human DMs would report (mirror of the AS-6 cli test at export.test.js:240-272). Falsifier: same reverted mutant; the counts test goes red.
AC-3. The existing assertion at export.test.js:123 (which today asserts dm-agent~cto-owen~~human~forrest.jsonl IS present) is inverted, not deleted — it becomes the regression pin for this task, and the '~ scheme applied' case on line 122 is re-pointed at an agent-agent key so it still exercises the filename mapping.
AC-4. A second human identity (e.g. human:test-advisor, registered in the test) in a DM with an agent is excluded by the same predicate — the falsifier for decision 1. If the implementation hard-codes 'human:forrest', this test goes red.
AC-5. The nine files are removed from the branch ('git diff --stat master...feat/AS-N-*' shows nine deletions under apps/chat/data/export/), and after merge a fresh './apps/chat/chat export' against the live DB re-creates none of them and leaves 'git status' clean for apps/chat/data/export/ apart from legitimately appended public files. The reviewer runs that export against a scratch copy of the DB, not the live one.
AC-6. Re-running export twice on the same DB is byte-identical (existing determinism test still green).
AC-7. apps/chat/README.md Durability section names the DM exclusion alongside the private-channel one, with the 'only durable copies are the live DB and manual dumps' tradeoff stated for DMs too.

BOARD GATES HIT: none. No spend, no external service, no CLAUDE.md edit (the pending-task note under 'Operational record commits' is the metawork layer's to close; propose the closing wording in a comment).

NOT IN SCOPE: rewriting history; excluding agent-agent DMs; changing #board/#bizdev handling; a private records repo (recorded alternative in CLAUDE.md 'Repo Visibility', board's call, not engineering's); redacting human authorship from public channels (human:forrest posts in #announcements/#engineering are public by design and stay exported).
data.title: Chat: exclude DMs involving a human (human:forrest) from the JSONL export exactly like #board/#bizdev — and delete the nine committed dm-*~~human~forrest.jsonl files

data.body:
PROPOSED CLAUDE.md WORDING (employees never edit CLAUDE.md — the orchestrator applies this; board directive DM msg 557, 2026-09-07). Insert as a new subsection under 'Lattice', after 'Creating Tasks'. Heading line, verbatim: '## Scheduling priority (board directive, DM msg 557, 2026-09-07)'. Body, verbatim:

After in-flight work completes its current lifecycle, every open task on the chat app and its tooling — titles beginning 'Chat:', plus the watcher/harness follow-ups under apps/chat (the AS-75 F-series AS-84..AS-88, AS-81, AS-82, AS-61) — is scheduled before any further D1 core-product task (AS-46/47/48/49/50/69/70/71 and AS-90's build stage), unless the board exempts a specific task in writing. 'In-flight' at the time of the directive means AS-45 (cycle 4) and AS-75 (in review): a task already in_progress or review finishes, it is not pre-empted. The Chat set carries priority high in Lattice so 'lattice next' reflects the rule; a tick that would otherwise start a D1 task while any Chat-set task is ready picks the Chat-set task instead and says so in its report. The rule lapses when the Chat set is empty or when the board lifts it in writing.

Enumerated set at time of writing (16): Chat:-titled AS-28, AS-72, AS-73, AS-74, AS-80, AS-83, AS-89, AS-91; chat-adjacent AS-61, AS-81, AS-82, AS-84, AS-85, AS-86, AS-87, AS-88. Deliberately OUT: AS-55 (tick permission grants, board-gated watcher config) and AS-79 (observability, board-gated external service) — flagged to the board as boundary cases in the DM reply.

provenance.reason: DM msg 557: Chat-first ordering (see AS-28 reason); also a recurring privacy leak on every export tick

data.body:
OPEN QUESTION CLOSED. The question in DM msg 565 (is AS-90 exempt from Chat-first?) was answered by the board in DM msg 567: 'do chat first' — AS-90 is not exempt (recorded on AS-90 on the board's behalf). Proposed CLAUDE.md replacement, for the metawork layer to apply (employees do not edit that file), for the sentence under 'Scheduling priority' that begins 'Open question put to the board in DM msg 565' — verbatim: Resolved 2026-09-07 by the board in DM msg 567 ("do chat first"): AS-90 is not exempt; it enters its lifecycle after the Chat set is empty and AS-45 has merged.

NEXT-TICK PICK. I checked whether Lattice itself can make 'lattice next' return AS-91: global 'lattice next' returns AS-61 (same critical priority, older — age tiebreak); 'lattice next --actor agent:developer-marcus' returns AS-28 (an older task already assigned to him). There is no priority above critical and no honest edge to add — AS-61 does not depend on AS-91, and fabricating a depends_on to steer the picker would be false board state. So the next tick that starts new work picks AS-91 by the recorded rule in CLAUDE.md 'Scheduling priority', not by 'lattice next', and says so in its report. AS-91 starts once in-flight AS-45 cycle 4 has cleared (WIP stays 1 until the parallel-lanes spike ships). AS-75's merge is the board's call, asked plainly in DM 7 this tick; it is not on AS-91's critical path — but AS-84 (+AS-88) is AS-75's follow-up, so if AS-75 is still unmerged when AS-91 is done, AS-84/AS-88 wait and the set continues with AS-85. Ruled order within the set (DM 565): AS-91, then AS-84 + AS-88, AS-85, AS-86, AS-87, AS-82, then the remaining Chat: tasks; then D1 resumes, AS-90 included.

PLAN WRITTEN (.lattice/plans/task_01M1YBPZTA7902T95HT37N7TG8.md, master 54f1dfb). Branch feat/AS-91-export-exclude-human-dms, worktree .worktrees/AS-91. Description line refs verified against master: all hold except the AS-6 cli test spans export.test.js:240-284 (counts at 262-263), and the plan scaffold held a copy of the description rather than being empty. Approach: one SQL predicate in exportFiles() (store.js:839) — AND NOT (type='dm' AND (substr(dm_key,1,6)='human:' OR instr(dm_key,'|human:')>0)) — row-local so it fails closed; chat.js untouched (its counts iterate the same array it writes, so 2a/2b cannot drift). Four named tests T1-T4 are the falsifier set; the mutant (delete that one line in a detached scratch worktree) must go red on exactly those four. Two commits on the branch: code+tests+README, then the nine git rm's (enumerated in plan §4). THINGS NOT TO GET WRONG: (1) every quoted suite number comes from a compose run with --build and a visible Built line, project-scoped with -p asc-as91-<actor>, no --progress quiet; (2) the AC-5 scratch DB copy must take chat.db AND chat.db-wal AND chat.db-shm — chat.db alone is three days stale; (3) a mutation is asserted applied (grep count 0, git diff --stat) before its run means anything; (4) the human is always the SECOND dm_key component for agent-human DMs, so T3 includes a human-human DM to exercise the first-component branch.

Starting implementation in .worktrees/AS-91 on feat/AS-91-export-exclude-human-dms (developer-marcus). Building to the plan as written, including its four named falsifier tests and the --build receipt rule for every counted run.

IMPLEMENTED on feat/AS-91-export-exclude-human-dms, two commits, worktree clean. NOT signed off: no acceptance-grade suite number exists yet — Docker on this host is dead (below), so no compose --build receipt was obtainable this tick.

COMMITS. e816fe7 'exclude DMs with a human participant from exportFiles()' (store.js predicate + comment, four tests, README AC-7); ffbc41c 'remove the nine committed human:forrest DM exports' (data only). Predicate is the plan's verbatim SQL: AND NOT (type = 'dm' AND (substr(dm_key, 1, 6) = 'human:' OR instr(dm_key, '|human:') > 0)), ANDed onto the AS-6 clause. bin/chat.js untouched (AC-9: 'git diff --stat master...HEAD -- apps/chat/bin' is empty). Nine deletions and only those (AC-5 first half): 'git diff --stat master...HEAD -- apps/chat/data/export/' = 9 files changed, 83 deletions, 0 insertions.

TWO PLAN DEVIATIONS, both forced, both flagged for review. Plan §2 lists the AS-5 tests (42-111) and the AS-6 trio (190-238) as untouched; two of them could not stay untouched:
(1) 'export round-trips the messages table faithfully' seeded a message in a human:forrest DM and checks the export against dumpLines(), which is visibility-blind — under the new predicate it asserted that an excluded conversation was exported, i.e. it went RED. Fix: its DM is now agent:cto-owen<->agent:developer-marcus, same body with pipe/colon. Considered and rejected: filtering the human DM out of the 'want' side — that would make this test go red under the §3 mutant too, widening AC-8's expected failing set from four to five and confusing the cardinality signal.
(2) 'AS-6: the export header line format is unchanged (no visibility key)' opened a human DM as its ONLY DM. It stays green either way, which is the problem: with the predicate in, its sweep silently covers channel headers only and the DM header-key contract goes untested — a vacuous pass. Fix: agent:developer-marcus<->agent:cto-owen, one line, green under the mutant, so the failing set is unchanged.

MUTATION (M4) — RUN, RED OBSERVED, but on the HOST, not under compose. Recipe as in plan §3: detached worktree of ffbc41c, deleted the predicate line so the WHERE is exactly the AS-6 form. Mutation asserted applied BEFORE running: 'grep -c "instr(dm_key"' = 0 and 'git -C $S diff --stat' = 'apps/chat/lib/store.js | 4 +---' (one file). Failing set is EXACTLY the four named tests, nothing wider or narrower:
  x DM filenames use the ~ scheme, are safe, and never collide            (T1)
  x AS-91: a DM with a human participant produces no export file; ...     (T2)
  x AS-91: any human identity is excluded, not just human:forrest ...     (T3)
  x cli: AS-91 - chat export skips human DMs: no file, no counts, ...     (T4)
T4's failure is the counts assertion, '5 !== 4' — the mutant reports the human DM as a fifth conversation, exactly the number the plan predicted. Both re-pointed tests above stayed green under the mutant, as intended.

COUNTS (host 'node --test' in apps/chat, node v24.13.1, hermetic per the AS-24 rule-4 guard; NOT acceptance-grade, no Built receipt): master 103bddb baseline 283 tests / 283 pass / 0 fail; branch ffbc41c 286 / 286 / 0 (+3 = T2,T3,T4; T1 modified in place); mutant 286 / 282 / 4. Same total on green and red runs.

BLOCKER — DOCKER DAEMON IS FAILING EVERY WRITE ON THIS HOST. Reproducible, not transient, and not caused by anything in this task:
  docker network create      -> Error response from daemon: failed to update bridge store ...: write /var/lib/docker/network/files/local-kv.db: input/output error
  docker pull hello-world    -> error creating temporary lease: write /var/lib/desktop-containerd/daemon/io.containerd.metadata.v1.bolt/meta.db: input/output error
  docker build (FROM scratch)-> failed to solve: Internal: write /var/lib/docker/buildkit/containerdmeta.db: input/output error
  docker builder prune       -> failed to prune build cache: write /var/lib/docker/buildkit/metadata_v2.db: input/output error
'docker images' lists nothing while nine containers (incl. asc-chat-server-1, asc-invoicing-web-1) still run from images by id, so the VM's image/network/buildkit stores are unreadable-or-unwritable at the filesystem level. Docker.raw is 60G virtual / 28G actual with 36Gi free on the host volume (96% used). Every write path inside the VM EIOs; reads of already-running state still work.

WHAT THIS BLOCKS: the compose --build receipt run (plan §5, CLAUDE.md's AS-45 corollary) for BOTH the green and the mutant numbers, and the reviewer's AC-5 scratch-DB export (plan §7) — that is a containerized cli run, same daemon. Until the daemon is healthy no number from this task may be quoted as acceptance-grade, mine above included; they are dev-loop signal only.

WHAT I DID NOT DO, deliberately: restarting Docker Desktop would bounce asc-chat-server-1 (8347), asc-invoicing-web-1 (8348) and five unrelated containers of the board member's, and repairing/resetting the VM disk is a host action with data at stake. That is not an IC's call to make unilaterally — needs the board or the orchestrator. Suggested minimal remedy in order: (1) restart Docker Desktop and re-probe with 'docker network create'; (2) if it still EIOs, free host space and/or let Docker Desktop repair the disk. Once 'docker compose -f .worktrees/AS-91/apps/chat/compose.yaml -p asc-as91-marcus --profile tools run --rm --build test' emits a 'Built' line, the green run and the §3 mutant run both need re-running under it before review closes.

PLAN NITS (neither changes the work): §0 says 'five agent-agent DM files' remain in apps/chat/data/export/ — there are four (ceo-carla~cto-owen, ceo-carla~developer-marcus, ceo-carla~qa-priya, qa-fixture~qa-priya) plus four channel files and identities.jsonl; the nine to delete were exactly as enumerated. And §2's untouched list, per the two deviations above.

Need: a Docker Desktop restart or VM-disk repair by the board (host action, orchestrator-verified 2026-09-09T20:45Z). The daemon EIOs on every write (docker network create -> local-kv.db: input/output error) and on overlay2 reads (docker inspect/logs -> overlay2/.../lower: input/output error); docker images lists zero images while nine containers keep running from memory. Consequences: no compose --build run is possible, so AS-91 has no acceptance-grade receipt (host node --test is 286/286 branch, 282/286 mutant with exactly T1-T4 red — dev-loop signal only, per the AS-45 corollary); the AS-75 watcher cannot rebuild either, so NO apps/chat merge should land until docker writes work (a merge would deploy-fail into the 30-min cooldown, loudly but uselessly); asc-chat-server-1 and asc-invoicing-web-1 read 'unhealthy' only because the healthcheck exec itself EIOs — 8347 answers 200 on /api/loop-status, /api/build and /api/conversations. Risk on restart: the image store is unreadable, so containers may not come back until the store is repaired; the chat DB is safe on the host bind mount (apps/chat/data), and the chat image rebuilds from the repo (all inputs in git) — the watcher redeploys it unattended once docker can build. Five of the nine running containers are the board's unrelated projects, which is why nobody at the company restarted it. Implementation is complete on the branch (e816fe7, ffbc41c); the review stage starts as soon as the receipt run is possible.
